close_reason: Implemented delegated OCSP responder support (RFC 6960 §4.2.2.2) in pkix-revocation. New flow in OcspChecker: resolve_signing_key_for_response unifies ResponderId match + signature key resolution; checks issuer first (direct path), then scans basic.certs for a cert whose ResponderId matches and validates it as a CA Designated Responder (validate_delegate_responder_cert: same-CA issuance, id-kp-OCSPSigning EKU presence, validity at producedAt, CA signature on TBS). Five new Error variants added (#[non_exhaustive]): OcspResponderEkuMissing, OcspResponderEkuMalformed, OcspResponderCertNotIssuedByCa, OcspResponderCertExpired, OcspResponderCertSigInvalid. id-pkix-ocsp-nocheck documented but not enforced (single-shot checker never recurses). Trusted Responder (third RFC 6960 case) explicitly out of scope. Responder ID matching now happens during signing-key resolution (before signature verify) — two pre-existing tests that checked corrupted-byKey produces OcspSignatureInvalid updated to expect the more specific OcspResponderIdMismatch (semantic invariant 'corrupted byKey rejected' preserved; new variant is strictly more diagnostic). 7 new pyca-generated fixtures (gen_ocsp_delegated_fixtures.py): ca/leaf + good/no-eku/wrong-ca/expired-cert/bad-sig delegated responses. 6 new integration tests covering the happy path + each of the 5 rejection modes + delegated check_revocation_against_anchor. All 21 OCSP tests pass; no_std preserved; clippy clean -D warnings; dependent crates pass.
description:
## Why

Documented limitation in `pkix-revocation/src/ocsp.rs:37-51`: the OcspChecker only accepts responses signed directly by the issuer of the cert being checked. Real-world OCSP responses are routinely signed by a *delegated* OCSP responder cert — a separate cert issued by the same CA, carrying the `id-kp-OCSPSigning` EKU, used to keep CA root keys offline.

Without this, every commercial OCSP deployment fails (Let's Encrypt, DigiCert, etc.).

## What

Extend `OcspChecker` (`pkix-revocation/src/ocsp.rs`) to:

1. **Accept a separate OCSP signer cert** in the response. RFC 6960 §4.2.2.2: the response's `certs` field carries the signer cert when delegated.
2. **Validate the delegate's chain** back to the cert's issuer. The delegate cert MUST be issued by the same CA whose certs the responder is asserting status for; this prevents a rogue cert with the EKU from being accepted.
3. **Verify the delegate carries `id-kp-OCSPSigning`** EKU (`1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.9`).
4. **Verify the delegate's own validity period** at the time the response was signed.
5. **Optional: `id-pkix-ocsp-nocheck`** extension handling. When present on the delegate, callers MUST NOT check the delegate's revocation status (otherwise infinite recursion). When absent, callers MAY check (typically via a CRL).

## Acceptance

- [ ] OCSP responses with a delegated signer cert in the `certs` field validate correctly when the signer is a properly-issued OCSP delegate.
- [ ] Responses with a 'rogue' signer (signer cert lacks `id-kp-OCSPSigning` EKU) are rejected.
- [ ] Responses where the signer's CA chain doesn't match the cert-being-checked's CA chain are rejected.
- [ ] Signer's own validity window checked.
- [ ] No regressions on direct (issuer-signed) responses.
- [ ] `id-pkix-ocsp-nocheck` documented; recommend treating it as 'caller decides whether to check delegate revocation' — pkix-revocation does not auto-recurse.
- [ ] Documentation: rustdoc updated, limitation note in `ocsp.rs:37-51` reflects what's now supported.

## Effort

Estimated ~120 lines + tests. ~1 day of focused work.

## Filed as

v1.0 'bar' item per gap audit. Pairs with indirect CRL for full revocation coverage. Required for any real-world commercial OCSP deployment.
title: pkix-revocation: delegated OCSP responder support (RFC 6960 §4.2.2.2)
